key_insight: Mesh-based graph neural networks capture neighborhood information, improving on local neural models for non-local closure prediction.
engineering_relevance: Using existing finite-volume mesh connectivity offers a practical route toward RANS closures that account for surrounding flow conditions.
method: Represent finite-volume cells as nodes and shared faces as graph edges.
Use GCN message passing so k layers incorporate information from k-hop neighborhoods.
Train on breadth-first-search k-hop subgraphs to augment data and reduce per-graph processing cost.
evidence_signal: Against equal-size feed-forward networks, GCNs generalize better in a laminar periodic-hills transport benchmark and show modest, consistent gains in turbulent eddy-viscosity prediction at Re = 5600.
watch_item: The turbulent result is a proof of concept for eddy-viscosity prediction, not evidence of improved coupled RANS simulations.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network based non-local models: Toward application to RANS turbulence modeling
